issue.title: Linked-repo ToolRuns are recorded under the host project's identity: tool_project_identity() prefers SASE_PROJECT over the catalog's repo
issue.description:
Found while researching the sase tool E3/E4 epics (swarm researcher cld, 2026-09-24, athena).

`tool_project_identity()` in `src/sase/config/tools.py` returns `SASE_PROJECT` /
`SASE_PROJECT_NAME` before it looks at the checkout it is running in. Every SASE agent
exports `SASE_PROJECT=gh_sase-org__sase`, so when an agent runs `sase tool run check`
from inside a linked repo checkout (`sase/repos/linked/sase-core`, sase-telegram,
sase-github, sase-research-artifacts — each has had its own `check` catalog entry and recipe guard since E1.5
phase sase-16h.6), the ToolRun is recorded with:

- `run.project = gh_sase-org__sase`
- `fingerprint_before/after.project_identity = gh_sase-org__sase`
- `fingerprint.repos[0].identity = gh_sase-org__sase` (but `head` is the linked repo's commit)

The catalog, argv, inputs, and toolchain probes are the linked repo's. So the identity
labels are wrong even though the rest of the evidence is correct.

Measured on athena's ledger (`sase tool runs -a -j`, 638 runs, 2026-09-20 → 2026-09-24):
51 `check` runs from linked repos are labeled as the sase project. They are
distinguishable only by `definition_digest`:
18dc41c8ba… = sase-core (39 runs), a2f2a5c5d2… = sase-telegram (5),
c0a5d0cbc9… = sase-github (4), f53749ed24… = sase-research-artifacts (3). Their
fingerprint input patterns (`Cargo.lock`, `scripts/check.sh`, …) confirm the origin.

Why it matters:
- TYPICAL is keyed by `definition_digest`, so `sase tool list` durations stay separate.
  But anything keyed by (project, tool name) conflates sase's `check` with every linked
  repo's `check`: `sase tool runs -t check`, LAST, and the planned E3 failure triage
  (KNOWN/FLAKY evidence) and E4 receipts, which are both keyed on tool identity.
- sase-core's `check` behaves very differently from sase's. On identical complete
  fingerprints, 9 of 11 repeats flipped failed→succeeded (flaky Rust tests), while all 18
  of sase's flipped zero times. Mixing the two would corrupt flake evidence.

Root cause: identity is taken from the agent environment instead of from the repo that
owns the resolved catalog (`discover_project_root()` of the catalog). The fix is to
derive the run's project identity and the fingerprint repo identity from the catalog's
project root when a named tool resolves there, or from cwd for ad-hoc runs. Keep
`SASE_PROJECT` only as agent attribution.
Existing mislabeled rows can be left as documented history. Alternatively, they can be
relabeled by definition digest. Decide which in the fix.

task_type_fields.impact:
Every linked-repo ToolRun is misattributed in the machine ledger. This does not break
E1/E2 behavior today (stats are digest-keyed). It is, however, a prerequisite defect for
the planned E3 (failure triage) and E4 (receipts). Both key evidence on tool identity,
and they would mix sase's deterministic `check` failures with sase-core's flaky ones.
Research: research:202609/sase_tool_e3_e4_readiness__cld.md (written in the same turn).
task_type_fields.repro:
From a SASE agent shell (SASE_PROJECT=gh_sase-org__sase) in a sase workspace:

    cd sase/repos/linked/sase-core && sase tool run check
    sase tool runs -t check -j -n 1 | jq '.runs[0] | {project, definition_digest, fp: .fingerprint_before.project_identity, repo: .fingerprint_before.repos[0].identity, head: .fingerprint_before.repos[0].head}'

Observed: project/fp/repo all `gh_sase-org__sase`, while head is the sase-core commit
(e.g. 6d0d0e6d5c, the current sase-core-revision.txt pin) and definition_digest is sase-core's.
Expected: the sase-core project identity.
